clue.text: One in The Oaks treating broken limbs?

definitions.text: One in The Oaks treating broken limbs?

parts.words: One in The Oaks treating broken limbs?
parts.note: the surface suggests a vet at the Oaks horse race seeing to a horse's legs; really it is someone up among oak trees mending damaged branches

explanation.surface: A vet at the Oaks racecourse patches up an injured runner's legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a famous English flat race for fillies at Epsom, so 'limbs' looks equine; the limbs are boughs of real oaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist who prunes and repairs damaged branches is a tree doctor, cryptically described as tending limbs.

clue.text: Reject a method to support performer

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so this piece comes after the performer

parts.note: a turn is a variety performer or act on a bill
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: An agent rejects a technique meant to prop up an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone away is to refuse them entry, a phrasal-verb synonym for rebuff.

clue.text: Old flame bound to cross river for publicity

indicators.note: bound passes over the river, so in this down entry it is placed just beyond it

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
the Po is Italy's longest river
bound means certain, sure

explanation.surface: A former lover is determined to cross a river and get into the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Media attention given to someone is coverage, so the two words are synonyms in the press sense.

clue.text: One will visit celebrity music producer

indicators.note: the single letter calls in on, so goes inside, the celebrity word

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone will drop in on a famous record producer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian lute-like instrument makes music, so it is cryptically a producer of it.

clue.text: Music paper of low quality with upcoming issue

parts.note: a rag is a disreputable newspaper

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: A tabloid's music coverage will appear in the next edition.
explanation.definitionFit: The syncopated piano style of Scott Joplin is a genre of popular music.

clue.text: Short public schoolboy hugs soprano in state

indicators.note: the trimmed schoolboy word wraps round the soprano letter
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil of Eton College, the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A small Eton boy embraces a soprano in some state.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an elite private one. 'Short' cuts ETONIAN to ETONIA, which 'hugs' S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic republic is a sovereign country, so it fits the nation sense of the word.

clue.text: On-air rant about commentary on DVD extra?

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcast tirade concerning the commentary track on a DVD bonus feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice-over telling the story is what a commentary track on a disc extra often provides.

clue.text: In a good mood, having first small drink

indicators.note: the small letter is put at the front of the word for being cheerful

parts.note: up means cheerful, in high spirits

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful after a first little tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: To sip or take liquid in small mouthfuls is to drink, an old-fashioned verb sense.

clue.text: Plonks served up by men creates this

definitions.text: Plonks served up by men creates this

indicators.note: by means beside, so the men follow
in a down clue served up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: to plonk is to put something down heavily
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Cheap wine poured out by the lads leaves everyone in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns PUTS into STUP. Plonk is also cheap wine, so the whole clue describes what too much of it causes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken stupefied daze is what plenty of cheap wine produces, so the whole clue is the definition.

clue.text: Editor punches mostly rubbish nit-picker

indicators.note: the editor letters punch into, so go inside, the other word
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish

explanation.surface: An editor lashes out at a fussy critic whose work is mostly rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over tiny details, exactly what a nit-picker does: a synonym.

clue.text: Do it to Plant if rubbish written about record

indicators.note: the rubbish word is written around the record

parts.note: rot means nonsense
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: What to do to Robert Plant if a rubbish review is written of his latest record.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests Led Zeppelin's Robert Plant; it is a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a houseplant into a new container is what one does to it when it outgrows its pot.

clue.text: Be socially active and buy the drinks?

definitions.meaning: to circulate a lot and mix with many people
read as three words, to purchase a set of drinks for the group

explanation.surface: A sociable person both mixes widely and stands drinks for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means circulating socially; split with an article it means buying a pub round.

clue.text: Confident statement and reason it's wrong

indicators.note: wrong means set out incorrectly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes a bold claim and argues the reasoning is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful declaration of belief is a claim stated firmly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bustling activity seen by Royal Navy deck

indicators.note: the navy letters are seen beside, so after, the fuss

parts.note: ado means fuss, busy activity

explanation.surface: A flurry of work by navy crew on a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to decorate it, so the verbs are synonyms; the noun deck is the misdirection.

clue.text: Sort a selection of products for an auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a hearer, so the words are to be heard

parts.note: a range is a line of products on offer

explanation.surface: Organise a product line for an accountant checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like the accountant but means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order is to organise them, a straight synonym of the verb sort.

clue.text: Unit of length is reported measure of relativity!

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a meter, a measuring gauge, for a nan, a grandmother and so a relative: a nan-o'-meter

explanation.surface: A unit of length is said to measure Einstein's relativity.
explanation.walkthrough: Relativity suggests Einstein; it means being a relative, and a gauge for a grandmother would be a nan-o'-meter.
explanation.definitionFit: One billionth of a metre is a metric distance measure, so a unit of length.

clue.text: Bitter conservative cuts financial support

indicators.note: the letter cuts into, so goes inside, the support word

parts.note: aid is money given to help

explanation.surface: An embittered Tory slashes funding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, sour taste or caustic remark can be called acerbic, close in sense to bitter.

clue.text: Pasta and corn I am cooking with dash of anise

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are mixed up as in a recipe
a dash is just a drop, so only the first letter of the spice is taken

explanation.surface: A recipe of pasta and corn, cooked with a hint of anise.
explanation.definitionFit: The short tube-shaped noodle is a familiar type of Italian pasta.

clue.text: Mormons excited to tour European lavatory

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the European letter
excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Excited Mormon missionaries set out to tour a European toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges MORMONS, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A gents' toilet is a lavatory for males, so the phrase is a specific example.

clue.text: Go mad just like that? I've done the same!

definitions.meaning: to lose one's temper or composure suddenly
as an adjective, sudden or instant, as in a quick decision
the cry in the card game when two matching cards appear

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper suddenly, then cries that they did the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to crack, an instant decision, and the call in the matching card game.

clue.text: Airborne soldier shot by northern model

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a shot is an attempt, a go

explanation.surface: A paratrooper is shot by a northern model.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example to be copied is a model of excellence, a synonym.

clue.text: Writer with reputation could be Slormgorm?

parts.note: a pen is the tool that writes
a name is a reputation, as in making a name for oneself

explanation.surface: An author with a reputation could be this puzzle's setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Slormgorm is this crossword's setter, whose byline is an invented alias.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter's byline like Slormgorm is an assumed literary alias, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Clown I report after being messed around

indicators.note: messed around means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clown files a report after being messed about.
explanation.definitionFit: The sad white-faced figure of French pantomime is a stock clown character.

clue.text: A lesser thoroughfare in a foreign land?

parts.note: British secondary roads are lettered B, a grade below the main A routes, so B plus the word for a route

explanation.surface: A minor road found in some foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, A roads are main routes and B roads lesser ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overseas means being out of one's own country, so the adverb fits.

clue.text: Bird circling North Dakota's capital city

indicators.note: the bird surrounds the state letters

parts.note: a loon is a diving bird, the North American name for a diver
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: A bird circles the state capital of North Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Dakota's capital' suggests Bismarck; the capital is the UK's.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of the UK government is the British capital, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Space on the right side of British sweeper

indicators.note: the space word sits to the right of, so after, the British letter

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: Space on the right-hand side of a British cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled brush for cleaning floors is used to sweep, so it is a sweeper.

clue.text: Communist informer protecting English plant

indicators.note: the communist word wraps protectively round the English letter

parts.note: red is a nickname for a communist
grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A communist informant shields an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall waterside grass growing in marshes is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Famous tenor left with one after live show

indicators.note: the left and one letters come after the show

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A famous tenor left alone after a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a renowned Italian opera singer, so the definition names him by example.

clue.text: Experienced worker glad store'll get refurb

indicators.note: a refurb is a refurbishment, so the letters are refitted in a new order

explanation.surface: A seasoned employee is pleased the shop will be done up.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran who has long been doing a job is a seasoned hand, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Foremost of goers loves party that's excellent

indicators.note: foremost means the front letter of the word is taken

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, an O, so two loves are two Os
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The best of the guests loves a party that's great.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses delight, as in great or splendid, matching excellent as a cry.

clue.text: Academic completely over taking ecstasy

indicators.note: taking means removing, so the drug letter is taken away

parts.note: done means finished, completely over
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A lecturer is completely finished after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like it adds E but takes it away.
explanation.definitionFit: A university fellow or tutor at Oxford or Cambridge is called by this title, so academic fits.

clue.text: Element of men in suite I put straight

indicators.note: putting things straight means tidying them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A part of the men in a hotel suite that I tidied up.
explanation.definitionFit: The synthetic radioactive metal with atomic number 99 is a chemical element.
